chapter: Hines 1935-38, Gus Arnheim and Billy Eckstine
title: Joe Dixon, Lou Singer and the end of Arnheim's band
summary: Arnheim names his chums and then breaks up the band to take a California bank job.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Joe Dixon played alto and clarinet. Very good clarinet player. And, after he left that band, he went with Fred Waring, you know. He was a great clarinet player. I see him every once in a while now. He lives out in Oceanside, Long Island. And, he still is a very good player. The flute and the clarinet. Anyway, we had this little boy, this drummer, Lou Singer.

Yeah. He was a terrific drummer, man. Lou Singer, man. And, those were my hang out guys. And, anyway, finally, after the Hotel New Yorker, well, Gus called us in the room. He says, "Well, Gentlemen," he says, "I'm breaking up the band." He says, "Because I'm kind of getting tired of travelling." He was a very wealthy man. He was a millionaire.

And, his wife was a millionaire. And, a very lovely lady. He says, "So, I'm going to give up the road. I'm going out to California, Hollywood and I got a position as vice president of a bank out there."
